headline: Vinicius Junior extends Real Madrid contract to 2032, ending Arsenal speculation
summary: Star forward Vinicius Junior has committed his future to Real Madrid for another eight years. The extension quells rumors about his potential move, solidifying his role in the club's ongoing success.
details: Real Madrid announced on Thursday that star forward Vinicius Junior has extended his contract with the club until June 30, 2032. This long-term agreement puts an end to speculation linking him with other clubs, including Arsenal.

Vinicius Jr. joined Real Madrid in July 2018 at the age of 18. Since then, he has played 375 matches, scored 128 goals, and secured 14 titles, including two Champions League trophies and three LaLiga titles.

His contributions have been crucial, particularly in major finals. He scored in the last two Champions League finals won by Real Madrid, in Paris (2022) and London (2024), showcasing his impact on the biggest stages.

During his tenure, Vinicius has earned numerous individual accolades. These include The Best FIFA Men's Player Award 2024, Golden Ball of the Intercontinental Cup 2024, and Best Player of the Champions League 2023-2024. He has also been featured multiple times in the FIFA World XI and Champions League Team of the Season.

headline: Collecting funds during Friday sermon is impermissible, say Islamic scholars
summary: Islamic teachings emphasize complete focus on the Khutba, making the common practice of collecting donations during the sermon contrary to its etiquette.
details: Friday is a special day for Muslims, with the Khutba and prayer being significant acts of worship. However, a common practice in many mosques is collecting donations during the Khutba, raising questions about its permissibility in Sharia.

The Quran instructs believers to hasten to the remembrance of Allah and cease worldly transactions when called for Friday prayer, referring to both Khutba and Salat. This emphasizes the importance of focusing solely on the Khutba after the call to prayer.

Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) stressed complete silence and attention during the Khutba. He stated that even telling someone to "be quiet" during the Imam's sermon is considered an unnecessary act, indicating the high level of focus required.

Scholars deduce that if telling someone to be quiet is discouraged, then activities like taking out money, passing donation boxes, or counting money, which distract even more, are certainly against the spirit of the Khutba. Therefore, avoiding such actions is essential.

While charity is highly encouraged in Islam, every act of worship has its prescribed time and etiquette. Performing a voluntary act (like collecting donations) that compromises an obligatory or more important act (listening to Khutba) is not acceptable in Sharia.

Listening to the Khutba is considered obligatory (Wajib) for a worshipper, whereas collecting donations is voluntary (Nafl or Mustahab). Islamic jurists (Fuqaha) have thus instructed to refrain from any activities during the Khutba that disrupt attention.

To maintain the sanctity of the Khutba, mosque authorities should collect donations either before the Khutba begins or after the prayer concludes. Placing permanent donation boxes at entrances or making announcements before Juma prayers are also permissible alternatives.
